messages:
kevin_cs: Hey team — customer reported a sudden burst this morning and started getting 429s. They say burst credits went to 0 very quickly. Repro notes: many small chat calls (~50 rps for ~30s). Any quick mitigation?

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste a request id + approximate timestamp and a snippet of the 429?

kevin_cs: req=abc123, ~2026-03-14T10:12:07Z. Log line: `2026-03-14T10:12:07Z ERROR req=abc123 status=429 msg=RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED burst_credits=0`. They were doing short chats (~20-60 tokens) in parallel.

toni_eng: Short answer: sounds like per-customer burst credits were exhausted. Our smoothing/burst system refills credits at a fixed rate (credits_per_min) and caps max burst. If a spike exceeds "sustained rate + burst" you'll see immediate 429s.

sam_ops: Quick mitigation options: 1) toggle smoothing policy to lengthen the window, 2) temporarily raise the burst_capacity for that org, or 3) advise client-side backoff. If they need immediate relief, we can add a short override.

alex_support: Example CLI to bump burst capacity for org `acme` for 10 minutes (ops-only):

```
redwood admin override create --org acme --key burst_capacity --value 500 --ttl 600
```

That will let them absorb the spike while we investigate. Also recommend enabling `retry-after` handling on the client and exponential backoff with jitter.

toni_eng: For config tuning, two knobs matter: `burst_capacity` (how many credits can be spent at once) and `smoothing_window_sec` (how quickly usage is averaged for refill math). For these short, high-RPS bursts we usually set smoothing_window_sec=60-120s and increase burst_capacity 2-4x.

sam_ops: How to inspect current credit state (admin API):

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/acme/burst_state" | jq
# sample response: { "available_credits": 0, "max_capacity": 300, "refill_rate_per_min": 120 }
```

alex_support: Note: the 429 response includes `Retry-After` and `x-burst-remaining`. Ask the customer to include the full raw headers when they hit it next time. That helps us pinpoint whether they hit global rate or burst window.

deploy-bot: rollout-note: smoothing-algo v1.3 was deployed 2026-03-12 03:00UTC. No known regressions but flagged for follow-up if we see many customer bursts.

kevin_cs: OK will try: (1) create short override, (2) enable smoothing_window=90, (3) ask client to backoff with Retry-After. Will update after they test. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Thanks — if you want, open a support ticket with the req ids and I'll attach the admin traces. If override used, ping me and I can revert once traffic stabilizes.

kevin_cs: Will do, thx everyone
